content.text: I've reviewed the full termination scheme, which is contained entirely in paragraph 4 (p0016), and confirmed there are no prepaid fees, early-termination fees, or additional termination mechanics elsewhere in the agreement.

input.quote: Neither Party may terminate this Agreement during the Initial Term except as set forth in paragraph 4(b) or any Exhibit. Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other Party. Except for termination for material breach as detailed in paragraph 4(b), Kubient shall be entitled to all fees generated during the termination period regardless of which Party terminates the Agreement
input.rationale: Clause 4(a) sits at the playbook fallback and does not warrant a redline. (1) Customer convenience right: AP may terminate for any reason on ninety (90) days' written notice, which is within the fallback's 60–90 day window. The convenience right is suspended only during a twelve (12) month Initial Term; the detection guidance treats the absence of a Customer convenience right as a deviation only where the term is longer than 12 months, and the Initial Term here is exactly one year with 1-year auto-renewals thereafter. (2) No penalty: there is no early-termination fee, and Kubient's entitlement to "all fees generated during the termination period" is simply the revenue share earned during the 90-day notice run-off, not a termination charge, so it is well inside the fallback's 3-month cap. There are also no prepaid fees under this revenue-share model (clause 5 pays AP within 7 days of Kubient's receipt), so the preferred pro-rata refund mechanic is inapplicable. (3) Vendor side: Kubient cannot terminate for convenience during the Initial Term at all, and thereafter needs 90 days' notice — at, not below, the walk-away threshold of "fewer than 90 days". The one sub-element short of the fallback is that Kubient's post-Initial-Term convenience right is not expressly confined to the end of a renewal term, so it could in theory be exercised mid-renewal on 90 days' notice; that is a minor shortfall of the mirrored right AP itself enjoys, is noted rather than flagged, and could be tightened at renewal if we want end-of-term-only symmetry.
